newsitem.title: UK: LIFFE robusta coffee reverses, still lags NY.
newsitem.headline: LIFFE robusta coffee reverses, still lags NY.

text.p: LIFFE robusta coffee futures reversed earlier downward direction to finish Wednesday slightly higher but still failed to catch up with a rebound in New York.
"It turned around and rallied with New York, albeit at a much lesser extent," said one trader.

New York arabica coffee futures bucked weaker chart trend to march sharply higher on an early burst of speculative buying, aided by news Tuesday's talks aimed at ending a truckers' strike in Colombia had collapsed.
By the close, London's July managed just $7 higher at $1,662 a tonne after a high of $1,670. May gained $4 at $1,632.

The bulk of the day's volume of 5,794 lots was centred on May/July switches which saw trades between $25 and $29. This followed further liquidation in May and the roller-over into July ahead of May's first tender day on May 1.
While the fundamental picture for arabicas remained encouraging on supply concerns, the prospects for well-supplied robustas are less rosy.
Robustas are now trading at an unprecedented $1.40 a lb below arabica prices and traders expect the huge gap to remain for some time.
Immediately, the London market could stay around the middle of the current $1,600-$1,700 range basis July, with roaster support and origin selling keeping a lid on either direction.
LIFFE options volume totalled 1,571 lots, with just over 1,000 lots changing hands in July $1,900 and $1,750 calls.
There was also a large interest in July $2,000 calls as a protection against the Brazil frost risk.
